claim.cause: releasing the emptied source route before refreshing the destination route let a later index shift cause refresh() to update the wrong route, leaving the real destination's cached load stale and letting subsequent capacity checks under-count it

feedback.approach: I read the planner's modules to understand where capacity was enforced, then used pmdb to query the recorded trace for any route_stats call where load_kg exceeded the vehicle's capacity. This surfaced not just the final T-44 overload but many transient ones, so I traced apply_move calls targeting T-44 and used pmdb --show to inspect the call tree around the move that pushed T-44 to 1614 kg. Computing actual stop demands confirmed the capacity check should have rejected that move, which pointed to stale cached stats; a scripted scan of all relocate moves for mismatches between the intended target vehicle and the actually-refreshed vehicle found the exact corrupting event in _relocate.
feedback.key_step: Writing a small script over the --show output to detect relocate moves where the refreshed route's vehicle id didn't match mv.v2 — this directly exposed that release() reindexing caused refresh() to update the wrong route.
feedback.wasted_effort: Manually grepping through /tmp/full_show.txt for prior refresh calls on a specific route index by hand before switching to a scripted mismatch-detection pass; the manual approach was slow and a general query would have found it sooner.
pmdb_problems: The query language can't express 'self' field access or compare opaque objects directly, so finding stats mismatches (vehicle id vs expected) required falling back to --export-xml/--show text parsing instead of a pmdb query.

No way to correlate a call's position/index in a list argument across time (e.g. 'what was plan.stats[r2] right before this call') since plan/self are opaque objects without a __pmdb__ method; had to infer from printed route_stats/refresh results instead.
show functions and select syntax errors (e.g. forgetting the method regex slash syntax) gave a generic parse error without suggesting the regex form, which cost a retry.
pmdb_wishes: A way to query 'the Nth argument equals the Mth result of an earlier matched call' (sequence/index correlation across time) to directly detect the stale-stats pattern instead of hand-correlating via grep.
Support for simple arithmetic/string extraction across a returned list of tables (e.g. matching 'vehicle' field of the second list element) without needing --export-xml.
A hint in the error message when a pattern looks like a method call without the required /regex/ syntax.
other_wishes: A way to add __pmdb__ to NamedTuple-based classes without editing source (model.py's Route/Plan are opaque since they're plain classes, not NamedTuples) would have made correlating stats-to-route mismatches queryable directly rather than via text scanning.
Being able to pass a Python predicate/snippet directly to pmdb for cross-call scans (what I ended up doing externally with a regex script) would have saved time.

claim.cause: Route statistics were not refreshed after route reorganization, causing capacity checks to use stale data and allowing overloaded moves.

feedback.approach: I used pmdb to trace the execution and find where the capacity violation occurred (T-44 with 1614 kg). feedback.key_step: Computing that if the capacity check used a load ≤1544 kg but the final load was 1614 kg, the statistics must not have been refreshed after other moves. This pointed to the locate() method not calling plan.refresh().
